subject.title: fix(sessions): add try-catch wrappers around unprotected JSON.parse calls in session-accessor.sqlite.ts

question: Should a malformed canonical transcript row fail with actionable diagnostics and doctor repair, or may runtime reads silently omit it and continue with partial state?
rationale: The correct behavior determines whether OpenClaw prioritizes data integrity or lossy availability at its canonical session-state boundary; source inspection cannot safely choose that product and recovery contract.

options.title: Fail And Repair
options.body: Return a typed corruption failure, preserve row identity, block idempotent writes, and provide a doctor repair or quarantine path before normal runtime resumes.

options.title: Allow Lossy Reads
options.body: Permit omission only with explicit owner acceptance, visible diagnostics, aligned row/event snapshots, duplicate prevention, and documented recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Fail And Repair
recommendation.body: Return a typed corruption failure, preserve row identity, block idempotent writes, and provide a doctor repair or quarantine path before normal runtime resumes.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite migration tracker and accessor implementation history make this person the clearest owner of the canonical transcript-storage contract.
